_: Golden for the es.2_0td preset — D2 §9 1 and 12, D9 §3. The claim is about a breaker, not a fee: item 1 of the precedence, INV-1.

sources.periods: companiadeluz.es/info/tarifas/2-0 and ahorr.ai's P1/P2 glossary, read 2026-09-19: P1 (punta) is Monday to Friday on working days 08:00-24:00; P2 (valle) is 00:00-08:00 on those days plus all 24 hours of Saturdays, Sundays and national holidays. The BOE wording the pages quote: "Se consideran como horas del periodo valle todas las horas de los sabados, domingos, el 6 de enero y los dias festivos de ambito nacional" — which is exactly `holidays: exclude` on the P1 filter, so a holiday falls through to P2 (D2 §2).
sources.limits: ASSUMED as a default the flow offers, not as anyone's contract. 4.6 kW (230 V x 20 A) is D2 §6's ES default and stays the punta figure; 5.75 kW (230 V x 25 A) is the next normalised step and is the valle figure, because the documented 2.0TD saving strategy is a higher power in valle, when the washing machine, dishwasher and EV run, and a lower one in punta. Both are standard normalised potencias. A site enters its own pair in the flow.
sources.tolerance: D2 §4: the Spanish ICP trips at about 10 % over for 30 s, which is tolerance_pct 0.10 and tolerance_s 30.
sources.no_peak: HLD §8's ES row: peak component `NoPeak`, hard limit `ContractedPower({P1, P2}, trip)`. Spain bills potencia contratada per day, not a measured peak, so there is no capacity metric and no ceiling — the breaker is the whole constraint.
sources.windows_priced: 0: nothing is priced on a version with no peak, though the windows are still recorded (INV-11).

limits.why: a working weekday before 08:00 is still P2
